neighbours.label: 'hold'/'held' in the sense of keeping something together or in place (held together, holds up, holding back), the verb that predicts 'together', 'up', 'intact'
fire: Only a few rusty nails held the fence together after the storm.
Thick steel cables hold up the bridge over the river.
The old levee is holding back the river for now.
A single screw holds the shelf in place on the wall.
Her calm voice held the frightened team together during the crisis.
Strong roots hold the soil together on the steep slope.
These two beams are what holds the roof up.
Without glue, nothing would hold the model plane together.
quiet: Only a few members held a vote after the storm.
Thick crowds hold signs outside the court every day.
The old museum is holding an exhibition for now.
A single ticket holds a seat for you at the show.
Her calm voice held the attention of the frightened children.
Strong teams hold training camps on the coast.
These two jars are what holds the sugar and flour.
Without a permit, nobody can hold a party in the park.

notes: Probe: 'held it together' 0.94, 'held together' 0.36, 'holding against flood' 0.35; 'held a meeting' 0.06, 'hold the door' 0.05. Output suppresses (- side promotes) 'together', 'up', 'intact', 'back'.
